text:
Jordan (support): heads up — multiple customers in us-west reporting p95/p99 tail spikes for embedding API since ~03:20 UTC. tickets: #7581, #7583. error rate small but latency huge.
Alex (eng-infra): thanks — any env rollout around that time? driver/firmware changes?
Jordan (support): customer says they saw our infra message about a scheduled driver push at 03:15 but not sure which hosts.
deploy-bot: Deploy finished: gpu-driver-rollout v2025.3 -> region: us-west at 03:18 UTC (hosts: gw-usw2-2[01-40]). :white_check_mark:
Maya (sre): pinging metrics — p95 embeddings backend spiked from 220ms -> ~1.8s at 03:22, p99 up to 4.6s. I/O wait on affected hosts increased.
Sunil (eng-runtime): that pattern matches hostfs/kv-cache writeback storms we've seen. Can we get iostat / pidstat from one affected host?
Katie (cs): I'm on call with the biggest customer, they're seeing tail latency for short queries only, long queries fine.
Alex (eng-infra): grabbing dmesg + iostat from gw-usw2-203 now.
Alex (eng-infra): paste: ```
03:24:12 iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s    w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s r_await w_await aqu-sz
nvme0n1         12.20  98.40   512.0  4096.0     0.00  0.00   2.15   5.10  0.12
nvme1n1          0.10  0.02     4.0     8.0     0.00  0.00  10.00 100.00  1.80
```
Alex (eng-infra): also `dmesg` shows repeated timeouts touching nvme1n1 around 03:20.
Maya (sre): interesting — nvme1n1 isn't our primary store for models but runtime sometimes thrashes small NVMe for kv-cache writes during eviction. Could driver update have changed scheduling?
Sunil (eng-runtime): driver v2025.3 included a new NVMe QoS patch that changed IO arbitration default. We added it to rollout notes but maybe opt-in flags flipped.
Jordan (support): customers asking for ETA/mitigation.
Maya (sre): immediate mitigations: 1) drain KV workload from affected hosts (move traffic) 2) disable kv-cache writeback on /dev/nvme1n1 by switching runtime flag `--kv-backoff=aggressive` 3) rollback driver to v2025.2 on most impacted hosts if needed. Thoughts?
Alex (eng-infra): I can start routing a portion of embedding traffic away from gw-usw2-2 pool — will create a split 20% -> fallback pool now.
Sunil (eng-runtime): I can flip `--kv-backoff=aggressive` via runtime config and push via feature flag to the swarm for the affected host tag. Command snippet: ```
redwoodctl cluster update --selector region=us-west,pool=gw-usw2-2 --set runtime.kv_backoff=aggressive
```
Alex (eng-infra): doing routing change now. hitting the traffic router: `routectl apply -f reduce-gw-usw2-2-traffic.yaml`
deploy-bot: Canary routing change applied, 20% traffic diverted at 03:31 UTC.
Maya (sre): after diversion I see p95 drop to ~360ms on majority, p99 still at 1.9s on remaining hosts.
Sunil (eng-runtime): config change rolling out to selected hosts. pushing in 3 waves.
Sunil (eng-runtime): config applied to first wave (gw-usw2-2[01-10]) at 03:36.
Alex (eng-infra): infra note — nvme1 SMART shows increased media wear warnings on 4 hosts, possibly coincidental but suspicious.
Maya (sre): suggest we isolate nvme1 usage: remount with `nobarrier`? probably not safe. better to evict kv-cache onto nvme0 or into RAM for now. Sunil?
Sunil (eng-runtime): can set runtime to prefer nvme0 for write-heavy cache: `runtime.cache.prefer_devices=[nvme0n1]` — applying to remaining hosts now.
Jordan (support): relayed to customers: "We've diverted traffic and adjusted cache settings, this should reduce tail latency. We're continuing investigation and will follow up"
Maya (sre): after full config roll, p95 back to 280-320ms, p99 under 700ms. Still seeing occasional 2s blips on 3 hosts.
Alex (eng-infra): starting rollback test on one host to driver v2025.2 to validate.
Sunil (eng-runtime): good. if rollback fixes the NVMe arbitration mismatch then we know the new driver patch is the root cause.
Alex (eng-infra): rolled back gw-usw2-2-07 -> v2025.2 at 03:52, immediate drop in local iowait and p99 fell to 420ms for that host.
Maya (sre): that points to driver QoS change as prime suspect.
Jordan (support): customers grateful — some asking for committed followup/patch timeline.
Alex (eng-infra): next steps: 1) halt further driver rollout in us-west 2) coordinate with driver vendor on reverting NVMe QoS default or add opt-out via config 3) schedule full rollback for affected hosts if vendor can't provide mitigation quickly 4) run targeted fio tests to reproduce writeback thrash.
Sunil (eng-runtime): I'll add a runtime defensive toggle to avoid kv-cache writes during heavy eviction windows and surface metric alerting for nvme write latency > 50ms.
Maya (sre): I'll open an incident postmortem draft with timeline and include command outputs, mitigation steps, and a mitigation-runbook.
Jordan (support): capturing customer impact numbers now for CS handoff.
Katie (cs): please include the CSP ticket ids and affected host list in the PM. I'll prep customer comms.
Alex (eng-infra): logging ticket with vendor: NVMe arbitration change in v2025.3 causing host-level writeback storms leading to p95/p99 spikes — attached fio reproduction and dmesg. ticket #DR-4921.
Sunil (eng-runtime): reproduction notes for postmortem: fio job: `fio --name=kv-evict --rw=randwrite --bs=16k --iodepth=32 --direct=1 --size=5G --numjobs=4 --runtime=600` against nvme1n1 while runtime doing continuous KV evictions. observed 1.8-2.5s latency spikes.
Maya (sre): status: mitigated (traffic diversion + runtime changes + targeted rollback). Severity reduced to P3. Will keep monitoring 24h.
Jordan (support): closing customer-facing "investigating" banner, switching to "mitigated" with follow-up note.
Alex (eng-infra): adding hosts to maintenance window for full rollback if vendor patch ETA > 48h.
Sunil (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add kv-cache device preference and a throttling knob.
Maya (sre): thanks team. postmortem draft ETA: 24h.
Katie (cs): thanks — I'll sync with account teams and legal for SLAs/credits if needed. :handshake:
Jordan (support): closing thread — will paste postmortem link when ready.
